Bitcoin (BTC) Explained Simply

Bitcoin is the world’s first decentralized cryptocurrency and the foundation of the entire crypto industry. It was created to enable peer-to-peer value transfers without banks or intermediaries, using blockchain technology for transparency and security. Bitcoin has a fixed supply of 21 million coins, which makes it deflationary and often referred to as “digital gold.” BTC is widely accepted and trusted, serving both as a means of exchange and a long-term store of value. Its proven security, decentralization, and limited supply make Bitcoin a cornerstone of modern digital finance.
